caption:
3 deaths and 1,262 hospitalisations in just 24 hours. Dengue continues to hit Bangladesh hard.

Three people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, from Thursday morning to Friday morning, according to the DGHS.

A total of 1,262 patients were admitted to hospitals during this period, bringing the total number of hospitalizations this year to 133,367.

Of those admitted, 126,713 patients have been discharged, while 6,236 people remain hospitalized.

The data was released on Friday (October 30) by the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Separately, reports indicate a measles outbreak with the death toll reaching 1,251, with two more deaths recorded in the last 24 hours.

headline_marked: Ex-airman [[jumped into Turag River while fleeing]] men in uniform, says friend
headline: Ex-airman jumped into Turag River while fleeing men in uniform, says friend
summary: PBI is investigating the death of former Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri after his friend claims they were chased by uniformed men.
details: Former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri died after jumping into the Turag River on October 27. His body was recovered from the Rajabari ferry terminal area on October 28.
Tahsif's friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who was taken into custody for questioning, told the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) that several people in uniform chased them near the riverbank.
Dip claimed that while they were talking at Mazar Basti, the uniformed men began chasing them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.
PBI investigators visited the site and recovered a motorcycle from the area, which they are currently verifying to see if it belonged to Tahsif.
A local tea stall owner reported that the motorcycle had been parked on the road for two days before police took it away.
CCTV footage showed Tahsif and Dip together shortly before Tahsif disappeared on the evening of October 27.
PBI is conducting a shadow investigation alongside the River Police to determine the exact circumstances of the death.
Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has demanded a fair investigation into the death of his son.
caption:
An ex-airman jumped into the Turag River to escape men in uniform, according to his friend.

Former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri died after jumping into the Turag River on October 27. His body was recovered from the Rajabari ferry terminal area on October 28.

Tahsif's friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who was taken into custody for questioning, told the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) that several people in uniform chased them near the riverbank.

Dip claimed that while they were talking at Mazar Basti, the uniformed men began chasing them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.

PBI investigators visited the site and recovered a motorcycle from the area, which they are currently verifying to see if it belonged to Tahsif.

A local tea stall owner reported that the motorcycle had been parked on the road for two days before police took it away.

CCTV footage showed Tahsif and Dip together shortly before Tahsif disappeared on the evening of October 27.

PBI is conducting a shadow investigation alongside the River Police to determine the exact circumstances of the death.

Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has demanded a fair investigation into the death of his son.

#Bangladesh #TahsifSouri #PBI #Investigation #Justice

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV
